H01.description: Imports shlex for the shell-quoted calibrate hint added by the D2 fix.

H02.description: Imports the single-source EFFORT_LEVELS constant; same values as before.

H03.description: Imports adapter_class_for_type for the adapter-derived effort_on_wire fix.

H04.description: Head has no planner for agy hops: with hounfour.headless.agy_opt_in off, a gated gemini-headless hop inside a mixed fallback chain stays in models_requested and is dispatched/walked as a failed hop instead of being planned around (the hunk also adds the CLI-aware calibrate hint used by D2).

H05.description: The observed provider-limit lookup ignores the hop's context_window, so a recorded observation outside the plausible window range (e.g. from a different route) can lower or set the input bound; intent inferred from the added argument.

H06.description: Replaces the local effort tuple with the shared constant of identical values.

H07.description: Docstring update describing the CLI-only 'both' warning.

H08.description: The 'sets both params.default_effort and extra.effort' warning fires for HTTP entries whose extra rung is never read, a misleading config warning.

H09.description: The CLI extra rung only reads the first truthy of extra.effort/reasoning_effort, so an invalid extra.effort hides a valid reasoning_effort and the invalid value is silently ignored without a warning.

H10.description: effort_effective is derived by a hard-coded provider check (any CLI hop passes effort through, only provider 'anthropic' maps) rather than the dispatching adapter, so the MODELINV record misstates the wire effort for codex/grok/other adapters and for providers whose block type differs from the key.

H11.description: A single-entry chain refused by the agy opt-in is reported with verdict reason 'Other' instead of a distinct OptInRequired reason.

H12.description: models_requested is taken from the full resolved chain without first planning around agy hops gated off by the opt-in, so gated hops are dispatched and counted.

H13.description: Pre-flight gate looks up the observed limit without the head entry's context_window, so implausible observations are not filtered.

H14.description: Passes models_not_planned to the exit-7 MODELINV emit.

H15.description: A CLI hop's own size rejection is recorded in the observed-ceiling store, lowering the HTTP route's input bound with a measurement that does not apply to it.

H16.description: The calibrate hint names the CLI hop's model (which the probe refuses) and interpolates the model id unquoted into a shell command the operator pastes.

H17.description: The preflight line always prints 'run: <probe command>' even for a CLI hop with no calibratable HTTP entry.

H18.description: The error JSON always says 'calibrate: <command>' even when no probe command applies.

H19.description: Per-hop bound computation looks up the observed limit without the hop's context_window.

H20.description: An agy-alone chain refused by the opt-in is recorded with error_class UNKNOWN and no failure_class, and the error JSON drops the failure_class, so consumers cannot tell it from a real failure.

H21.description: effort_effective is computed inline inside the emit call, so any exception in its derivation falls into the emit's handler and the whole MODELINV envelope is lost.

H22.description: Inline effort_effective derivation inside the emit call can raise and lose the envelope (fix also passes models_not_planned).

H23.description: argparse choices use the shared EFFORT_LEVELS constant (same values).

H24.description: Emitter signature gains models_not_planned for the agy planning fix; comments updated.

H25.description: Docstring lists provider and failure_class keys.

H29.description: _HAS_YAML flag (fallback branch) for the strict opt-in reader.

H30.description: agy_opt_in_enabled lets the framework System defaults satisfy the operator opt-in, reads the config from whatever cwd-ancestor root the walk finds (a planted .loa.config.yaml can opt in), accepts PyYAML 1.1 truthy spellings (yes/on/True) and never checks that the config is writable only by the current user, so the argv-exposing agy route can be enabled without the operator's decision.

H31.description: validate_config keeps checking type and the agy binary when the opt-in is off, adding irrelevant 'CLI not found' errors to the opt-in refusal.

H32.description: Imports ProviderContextLimitError for the size-rejection classification.

H33.description: build_headless_argv accepts a prompt and places it right after -p before the options, so a prompt starting with '-' is parsed by the CLI as a flag.

H34.description: Docstring update for the stdin-only builder.

H35.description: The argv prompt is inserted in option position (before --output-format etc.), where a leading '-' is parsed as an option.

H36.description: Static-auth marker list used by the new error classification.

H37.description: Adds the wire_effort hook consumed by the adapter-derived effort_on_wire.

H38.description: Caller updated for the builder that no longer takes a prompt.

H39.description: No option terminator: an argv prompt is never placed after '--', so a prompt beginning with '-' can be read as a CLI flag.

H40.description: The CLI's own 'Prompt is too long' size rejection is not mapped to a context-limit error, and bare '429'/'529' substrings (e.g. digits inside a stated token count) classify it as a retryable rate limit that walks the chain and counts against breakers; a 'please wait' auth message is also treated as a throttle.

H41.description: Adds 'invalid api key' to the static-auth markers, matching the new marker list.

H43.description: ConfigError accepts a context so the opt-in failure_class flows through the base constructor.

H44.description: AgyOptInRequiredError passes its failure_class context through the base constructor so cheval can read it; intent beyond the D9 fix is unclear from the context.

H91.description: Free-text ceiling_calibration strings (reprobe_trigger, cli_version, cli_model) have no length bound in the schema.

H92.description: Unbounded ceiling_calibration string field in the schema.

H95.description: The schema neither records nor requires a probe outcome for a probed_headless bound, so a partial (budget-capped) probe is indistinguishable from a clean one in the catalog.

H96.description: Schema admits the new models_failed[].failure_class field.

H100.description: The probed Opus 5.5 entry records sample_size: null although a probe with samples informed the bound.

H103.description: Sources the shared agy-gate lib used by the predicate fix.

H104.description: The companion planner only drops a hop whose canonical name is exactly gemini-headless, missing agy-routed hops (provider-prefixed forms, Google models under cli-only, project aliases), and its own yq reader differs from the shared strict opt-in rule.

H105.description: The dissent planner never emits the once-per-run gate warning when the agy route is available but gated.

H107.description: Flatline's tertiary agy predicate uses its own name/gemini* heuristic (no catalog aliases such as deep-research-pro) and a separate yq reader instead of the shared rule, so agy-routed tertiaries can be misjudged.

H108.description: Flatline never emits the once-per-run agy gate warning.

H110.description: /loa status uses its own opt-in reader and a provider=='google' heuristic rather than the shared agy route predicate, so its gate note can disagree with cheval.

H111.description: The CLI hop gating keys on the binary name agy rather than the shared routes_to_agy predicate.

H112.description: The ceiling line splices the alias-derived model id into yq expression text, accepts observations outside the plausible window, ignores a foreign-transport calibration that an observation should tighten, and prints an unquoted calibrate command.

H113.description: The Providers section never emits the agy gate warning.

H114.description: Renders the new calibrated-but-observed-below ceiling basis.

H117.description: cli_for ignores provider-prefixed ids (google:gemini-headless) and the local opt-in reader uses python-yq '== true', which differs from the strict shared rule.

H118.description: provider_of returns no provider for catalog model ids without a family prefix (e.g. deep-research-pro), so such Google voices are not recognised.

H119.description: Precomputes mode/opt-in for the shared predicate and emits the gate warning.

H120.description: P3 gates only hops whose CLI is agy, so a Google model under cli-only (routed through agy) is counted usable on its Google credential with the opt-in off, and when opted in its usability is judged by the credential instead of the agy binary.

H121.description: A stage whose every voice is gated off by the opt-in is reported as having no credential and no CLI on PATH, a misleading failure reason.

H122.description: The P3 FAIL detail gives the missing-credential reason for stages that failed only because of the agy opt-in.

H158.description: Bridgebuilder's readAgyGate defaults to the cwd config, never checks the config's owner/permissions, reads through aliases/merge keys without warning, swallows every read error silently as opt-in off, and isAgyRouted only matches the literal gemini-headless id.

H159.description: Removes the cwd default gate parameter so callers pass the repo config.

H160.description: When the Loa config cannot be read, Google voices are still planned as HTTP voices although cheval may route them to agy and refuse them, so the failure is miscounted.

H161.description: Adds startup lines for the read error / type warning.

H163.description: An unreadable config or a non-boolean opt-in is logged only as 'agy opt-in off' at info level, and strict mode silently runs without a configured voice instead of warning or refusing.

H164.description: With no usable model the error always says 'all API keys missing' even when the voices were removed by the agy gate.

H165.description: The posted verdict header never names the voices that were not planned or why.

H166.description: Voices removed by a config read error shrink the expected quorum, so a review missing them can still clear the merge.

H168.description: The verdict quality line omits the not-planned voices.

H170.description: The Opus 5.5 budget (916000) takes a ceiling measured in provider tokens as estimate-unit tokens, and the char estimator under-counts the tokenizer ~1.8x, so Bridgebuilder builds prompts far past the real window.

H198.description: math/re imports for the classifier fixes.

H199.description: traceback import for the interrupted-record handling.

H200.description: A tokens-per-minute 429 is retried on the 5 s/15 s schedule, which cannot clear the 60 s window, and after three attempts it is recorded as a size rejection, so the probe can bracket the ceiling with a throttle.

H201.description: The 5xx regex matches any bare three-digit 5xx number (e.g. 'took 503 ms'), so non-transient failures are retried as transient.

H202.description: Operator- and CLI-supplied strings (host route, resolved cli model, cli --version) reach the catalog's provenance text unchecked, so a control or line-break character can break or inject YAML into the catalog.

H203.description: subprocess.run(timeout=) kills only the direct child (the wrapper), leaving the claude process running, and output past 1 MB is silently truncated and still classified.

H204.description: An exception inside classification propagates and aborts the probe, losing the record of paid steps.

H205.description: Usage and cost values from the CLI JSON are taken unchecked; Infinity/NaN or absurd values crash the cost arithmetic (OverflowError) and lose the record.

H206.description: Classification runs on a 300-character truncated diagnostic and checks the context-limit marker before throttling, so Bedrock's 'Too many tokens, please wait' throttle is recorded as a size rejection and markers past 300 chars are missed.

H207.description: Transient markers are searched in the truncated diagnostic only.

H208.description: Writer signature gains the required probe_outcome/sample_size parameters.

H209.description: write_catalog_operator_set takes no probe outcome or sample count and does not validate its string inputs, so a written entry cannot say whether its probe was clean or partial.

H210.description: The catalog writer hard-codes sample_size: null and writes no probe_outcome.

H211.description: Provenance comment gains the partial note via a template.

H212.description: The produced catalog text is returned without re-parsing, so a malformed or collateral edit is written unverified.

H213.description: Argument defaults/help changed so api-only flags can be detected; adds the partial-write flag.

H215.description: An outcome bracketed by a token-limit (throttle) rejection rather than a context-limit rejection is accepted as clean, so a rate limit is written as the context ceiling.

H216.description: Spend accounting charges every failed attempt the full estimate (including the CLI's free local pre-flight rejections and never-sent spawns), exhausting the budget cap on attempts that cost nothing.

H217.description: Usage check for the new partial-write flag.

H218.description: With --write-catalog the catalog prerequisites (block, context_window, writable file) and the provenance strings are only checked after the paid bisection, and the cost estimate ignores the cache-write rate and tokenizer ratio, so money is spent on a probe whose write cannot land.

H219.description: The budget pre-check estimates the first step at ratio 1.0, under-estimating its cost by the ~1.8x tokenizer ratio, so the cap can be exceeded.

H221.description: A token-limit transient that persists over the short retries is turned into a size rejection without the TPM window having been waited out, and output-cap/timeout/spawn cases are not distinguished for charging.

H222.description: A ^C or unexpected exception during the bisection aborts without writing the record of the paid steps.

H223.description: Adds the interruption reason to the outcome reasons.

H224.description: The record stores the binary path and argv with the operator's absolute home path (and an unresolved bare binary name).

H225.description: The record claims written_ceiling before the catalog write is attempted, so a failed write still leaves a record saying it was written.

H226.description: No exit path distinguishes an interrupted probe; with the record lost on exception the operator gets no record or exit status for it.

H227.description: Catalog write moved before the record is serialized.
